BiblicalUsage: Once, in the border of Asher: the coast turns to Carmel westward, and to Shihor-libnath, and then to Allammelek, and Amad, and Mishal, and reaches to Carmel westward. The name is a town on the boundary line, and the boundary is all the Bible says of it.
TheologicalSignificance: A town named once on a border carries no lesson of its own. What it shows is the care of the record, that even the boundary towns are named, and the inheritance is measured town by town.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
